stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site and $K^\bullet$ a complex of $\mathcal O$-modules. Here $(E,\mathrm d)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Comp}^{dg}(\mathcal O)}(K^\bullet,K^\bullet)$ is the differential graded endomorphism algebra of $K^\bullet$.

The dg functor $M\mapsto M\otimes_E K^\bullet$ from $\operatorname{Mod}^{dg}_{(E,\mathrm d)}$ to $\operatorname{Comp}^{dg}(\mathcal O)$ defines an exact functor
of triangulated categories
$K(\text{Mod}_{(E, \text{d})}) \to K(\mathcal{O})$.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site; K is an O-module complex; E is its dg endomorphism algebra.
conclusions: The dg functor M↦M⊗_E K induces an exact triangulated functor from K(Mod_E) to K(O).

reason: A dg functor descends to homotopy categories. Tensoring any admissible graded-split short exact sequence of E-modules with K remains a degreewise split sequence of O-complexes, hence produces the requisite distinguished triangle and exactness.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site and $K^\bullet$ a complex of $\mathcal O$-modules. Here $(E,\mathrm d)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Comp}^{dg}(\mathcal O)}(K^\bullet,K^\bullet)$ is the differential graded endomorphism algebra of $K^\bullet$.

The functor $K(\text{Mod}_{(E, \text{d})}) \to K(\mathcal{O})$
induced by the dg tensor functor $M\mapsto M\otimes_E K^\bullet$ has a left derived
version defined on all of $D(E, \text{d})$. We denote it
$- \otimes_E^\mathbf{L} K^\bullet : D(E, \text{d}) \to D(\mathcal{O})$.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site; K is an O-module complex; E is its dg endomorphism algebra.
conclusions: The homotopy-level tensor functor has a left derived functor on all D(E), denoted -⊗_E^L K:D(E)→D(O).

reason: The class of property-(P) dg E-modules provides quasi-isomorphic resolutions of every object, and quasi-isomorphisms between these are homotopy equivalences. These conditions satisfy the cited derived-functor existence/computation criterion, yielding the left derived tensor on all of D(E).

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Convention: a ring is commutative with $1$; an $R$-algebra is associative, unital and central over $R$.

Here $(E,\mathrm d)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Comp}^{dg}(\mathcal O)}(K^\bullet,K^\bullet)$ is the differential graded endomorphism algebra of $K^\bullet$.

Let $R$ be a ring. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\mathcal{O}$
be a sheaf of commutative $R$-algebras. Let $K^\bullet$
be a complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
The derived tensor functor $-\otimes_E^{\mathbf L}K^\bullet:D(E,\mathrm d)\to D(\mathcal O)$ has the following
property: For every $M$, $N$ in $D(E, \text{d})$ there is a
canonical map
$$
R\Hom(M, N)
\longrightarrow
R\Hom_\mathcal{O}(M \otimes_E^\mathbf{L} K^\bullet,
N \otimes_E^\mathbf{L} K^\bullet)
$$
in $D(R)$ which on cohomology modules gives the maps
$$
\Ext^n_{D(E, \text{d})}(M, N) \to
\Ext^n_{D(\mathcal{O})}
(M \otimes_E^\mathbf{L} K^\bullet, N \otimes_E^\mathbf{L} K^\bullet)
$$
induced by the functor $- \otimes_E^\mathbf{L} K^\bullet$.
hypotheses: R is a commutative unital ring, C a site, O a sheaf of commutative R-algebras, K an O-complex, E its dg endomorphism algebra; M and N are objects of D(E).
conclusions: There is a canonical derived-Hom comparison map in D(R) from RHom_E(M,N) to RHom_O(M⊗_E^L K,N⊗_E^L K), inducing the Ext maps of derived tensor.

reason: After property-(P) replacements, the dg tensor functor induces a chain map from dg Hom_E(M,N) to dg Hom_O(M⊗_E K,N⊗_E K). The natural map from global ordinary Hom complexes to global RHom then gives a canonical morphism in D(R); on cohomology it is the Hom/Ext map induced by the derived tensor functor. Source uses stray A/B names instead of E in intermediate formulas.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Here $(E,\mathrm d)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Comp}^{dg}(\mathcal O)}(K^\bullet,K^\bullet)$ is the differential graded endomorphism algebra of $K^\bullet$.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $K^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Then the functor
$$
- \otimes_E^\mathbf{L} K^\bullet :
D(E, \text{d})
\longrightarrow
D(\mathcal{O})
$$ is a left adjoint
of the functor
$$
R\Hom(K^\bullet, -) : D(\mathcal{O}) \longrightarrow D(E, \text{d})
$$.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, K an O-module complex, and E its dg endomorphism algebra.
conclusions: The derived tensor -⊗_E^L K:D(E)→D(O) is left adjoint to RHom(K,-):D(O)→D(E).

reason: With property-(P) replacement P of M and K-injective replacement I of L, the adjunction reduces to the Hom_K pairing Hom_E(P,Hom_O(K,I))≅Hom_O(P⊗_E K,I). Both sides take sums to products and are homological in P; the property-(P) filtration reduces to E[k], for which the dg tensor–Hom pairing is immediate.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $K^\bullet$ be a complex of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $K^\bullet$ represents a compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$, and
\item $E = \Hom_{\text{Comp}^{dg}(\mathcal{O})}(K^\bullet, K^\bullet)$
induces isomorphisms $H^n(E)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(K^\bullet,K^\bullet[n])$ for all integers $n$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the functor
$$
- \otimes_E^\mathbf{L} K^\bullet :
D(E, \text{d})
\longrightarrow
D(\mathcal{O})
$$ is fully faithful.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site; K is compact in D(O); E is its dg endomorphism algebra and H^n(E) agrees with Hom_D(O)(K,K[n]) for each n.
conclusions: The derived tensor functor -⊗_E^L K:D(E)→D(O) is fully faithful.

reason: The derived tensor–RHom adjunction makes full faithfulness equivalent to an isomorphism of its unit on every M. Compactness of K and property-(P) resolutions reduce the cohomological unit test to free shifts E[k]; the assumed dg endomorphism/Ext identification proves it there. The phrase 'left adjoint' for RHom in the source proof is a directional typo.
